newsitem.title: USA: Computer Learning rebuffed in federal court.
newsitem.headline: Computer Learning rebuffed in federal court.

text.p: Computer Learning Centers Inc said Friday the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois had denied its motion for partial summary judgment in its suit against the U.S. Department of Education.

The company had asked the court to compel the government to recognize its Chicago Learning Center's 1994 preliminary student cohort default rate of 20.1 percent as representing the most recent cohort default rate data.
Recognition of this rate would have restored Chicago Learning Center's eligibility to participate in federally funded Family Education Loan and Federal Pell Grant programs.

The company said the court ruling does not affect Chicago Learning Center's ability to resume participation in the Pell program on July 1 and to reapply to resume participation in the Family Education Loan program on October 1.

Federal law regarding government-sponsored student loans state that any institution that posts three consecutive years of student loan default rates in excess of 25 percent may lose access to certain federally-funded student loan programs.
